evals.prompt: Can you do the seating for our anniversary dinner? 30 guests, three round tables of 10, guest list attached (guests.csv). Table 1 is the only step-free one. Keep households together, and please keep Cal Reed and Ivy Lowe apart — long story.
assertions: Seats all 30 guests, each exactly once, with no table over 10
Every household from the list sits at one table
Cal Reed and Ivy Lowe are at different tables
Rosa Vega, who uses a wheelchair, is at table 1
Leads with a table-by-table list of who sits where
Lists the dietary needs per table for the caterer
Saves a drawing of the room under a plain name in the working directory and names it
Does not mention scripts, JSON or the skill's own files in the reply

evals.prompt: Our venue coordinator sent this table plan (table-plan.txt). Can you check it before we print place cards? Don't redo it, just tell me what's wrong and how to fix it.
assertions: Finds that table 1 has 9 guests for 8 seats
Finds that Cal Reed and Ivy Lowe, who must not sit together, are both at table 1
Finds that Rosa Vega, who uses a wheelchair, is at table 2, which isn't step-free
Finds that the Ota household is split between tables 3 and 4
Gives a fix for each problem that moves as few guests as possible
Does not hand back a rewritten plan for the whole room
Does not invent guests, tables or requests that aren't in the file

evals.prompt: Seat the awards dinner (brief.txt, guests.csv). Northwind asked for all 12 of their people at one table. Non-interactive, no follow-up questions.
assertions: Says plainly that 12 people can't sit at one 10-seat table
Proposes the smallest change, such as splitting Northwind across two neighbouring tables or a larger table if the venue has one, and says which
Seats every other company's guests together by company
Seats every guest exactly once, with no table over 10
Does not quietly seat 12 at a table of 10 or drop guests to make it fit
States any assumption it made, tagged
